correctness.rationale: The Fourier quadratic-form identity reduces the deficit to a double integral with nonnegative phase gap. On \(|\xi|\le B\) and \(0<BT<1\), \(K_T(\xi)=T\sin(\pi T\xi)/(\pi T\xi)\) is bounded below by \(T\sin(\pi BT)/(\pi BT)\). Integrating the phase gap gives \(\|\widehat f\|_1^2-|f(0)|^2\) by Fourier inversion. Equal-mass opposite-phase packets near opposite endpoints make the ratio tend to the kernel minimum, proving the coefficient optimal. All hypotheses and the \(BT<1\) boundary are stated explicitly.

value.rationale: The result turns a qualitative phase-alignment inequality into a sharp quantitative stability estimate with explicit dependence on the time–bandwidth product. The right-hand side is a natural phase-cancellation invariant, equivalently the gap between the phase-aligned peak and the original central peak. The bound yields a weighted phase-coherence estimate for near-equality cases, and the endpoint-packet construction shows the constant is not an artifact of the proof.
